data.name: Nevin
data.gender_notes: Nevin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Nevyn, meaning 'comfort, solace'. Nevyn comes from the Hebrew verb 'nhan', meaning 'to comfort'. In the Bible, this name is associated with the prophet Nehemiah, who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem and brought comfort and restoration to the Israelites. The name Nevin carries the meaning “Comfort, solace” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nevin usually hope their child will grow to embody comfort, solace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes comfort, consolation, and hope.
data.etymology: Nevin belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Comfort, solace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nevin total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nevin, with its Hebrew origins, has strong historical and cultural associations with the Jewish people and the biblical narrative. This connection can provide a sense of rich history and heritage for those bearing this name. Moreover, the fact that Nehemiah is remembered for his leadership and ability to restore and rebuild makes Nevin an inspiring name, particularly for those who value strength, resilience, and the enduring power of community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nevin draws on the spiritual themes of comfort, solace, and restoration. In a Christian context, these concepts can be understood as an expression of God's compassionate presence and understanding in our lives. As Jesus said in the Gospel of Matthew, "Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). In this way, Nevin serves as a constant reminder that even in the most challenging of circumstances, the comfort and hope found in God are always available to us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nevin: Derived from the Hebrew name "Nathan," meaning "given," or "grace and favor." In Christian tradition, it symbolizes the divine gift of grace bestowed upon an individual, inspiring them to live a life of faith and obedience to God.

historical_references.reference: John Nevin (1803-1886): A Presbyterian minister and theologian, he was born in County Armagh, Northern Ireland. Nevin was a prominent figure in the early Presbyterian Church in the United States. He is best known for his influential work 'The Mystery of the Trinity', which helped to shape the theological landscape of the Presbyterian Church in America.
historical_references.context: Early Presbyterian Church in the United States

historical_references.reference: John McLeod Campbell (1838-1915), a Scottish-born Presbyterian theologian, was influenced by John Nevin’s theological thought. Campbell is recognized for his role in the development of the 'New School' of Presbyterianism in the United States. Nevin and Campbell's collaborative work 'Rational Theology: Or, the Doctrine of God' further solidified their impact on Presbyterian thought.
historical_references.context: Development of the 'New School' of Presbyterianism in the United States
